contributions.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' line 1 TOTAL CONTRIBUTIONS RECEIVED ($7,280.14) on the Summary Page (PDF p2), which equals the filer's own ledger footer 'Total Contributions Received $7,280.14' printed at the foot of PDF p4 and the sum of its two printed page subtotals (1,894.78 + 5,385.36)
contributions.detail: The filer replaced the county's Schedule A form with her own typed two-page spreadsheet, hand-headed 'Schedule A Itemized Contributions Received page 1/2' and 'page 2/2'. PDF p3 carries 47 rows summing to 1,894.78 = its own printed subtotal to the cent; PDF p4 carries 30 rows summing to 5,385.36 = its own printed subtotal to the cent; 1,894.78 + 5,385.36 = 7,280.14 = the ledger's printed grand total = the cover's promoted per-period Column A cell. THE IN-KIND CONVENTION IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE OTHER COMMISSION FILING IN THIS CHUNK: three rows are marked 'in kind' in the donor cell (Facebook 50.00, MG Graphic Design 1,845.36, Ann Bryner videos 1,000.00) and ALL THREE ARE INSIDE the printed subtotals — monetary-only would fall 2,895.36 short of 7,280.14, monetary-plus-in-kind closes exactly. Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints the same 7,280.14 and is never summed as an increment; the balance ladder is internally consistent (line 3 beginning 0 + line 4 7,280.14 = line 5 7,280.14; minus line 6 6,657.58 = line 7 622.56), and that ladder is what settles the hundreds digit of line 2, which is ambiguous between 5 and 6 as a glyph.

expenditures.anchor: Column A 'Total this Period' line 2 TOTAL EXPENDITURES MADE ($6,657.58) on the Summary Page, equal to the filer's own ledger footer 'Total Expenditures $6,657.58' at the foot of PDF p5
expenditures.detail: One typed ledger page, hand-headed 'Schedule B Itemized Expenditures page 1/1', 42 rows: 20.84+29.00+59.40+35.00+50.00+9.70+13.58+162.13+20.00+8.75+647.22+25.00+219.31+18.15+20.08+15.43+16.02+17.68+50.00+104.35+15.41+5.00+161.34+16.44+20.30+104.35+24.66+10.00+10.33+105.42+105.42+448.77+5.00+250.00+44.48+7.50+1845.36+855.00+12.58+25.00+1000.00+43.58 = 6,657.58 exactly = the printed total = Column A. The same three in-kind items appear here as OFFSETTING EXPENDITURES of identical date and amount to their contribution rows (Facebook 50.00 on 10-Jan-18; Megan Geilman Graphic Design 1,845.36 on 12-Oct-18; Ann Bryner videos 1,000.00 on 20-Oct-18) and are likewise INSIDE the printed total — the double-entry in-kind convention, and monetary-only would fall 2,895.36 short on this side too. Column B YTD prints the same 6,657.58 and is not summed. Line 2's hundreds digit is ambiguous as a glyph (5 vs 6) and was settled by ARITHMETIC, not by re-reading: the rows sum to 6,657.58 and the summary ladder closes only at 6,657.58 (7,280.14 - 6,657.58 = the printed 622.56).

in_kind_convention: monetary-PLUS-in-kind — tested on BOTH sides of THIS filing (§G1) and it is the convention that closes BOTH. The filer marks in-kind inside the name cell ('Facebook in kind', 'MG Graphic Design in kind', 'Ann Bryner videos in kind') and enters each gift TWICE, once as a contribution and once as an offsetting expenditure of identical date and amount, with both printed totals including them. Monetary-only fails by exactly 2,895.36 on each side. ⚠ This is the direct counter-example to the Ellingson filing in the same chunk and the same cycle, whose single in-kind row is EXCLUDED from its Column A — proof that the convention is a property of the filing, never of the form or the year.
escalation_note: The ledgers are machine-typed and every figure was legible at the 200 dpi full-page read; both sides close to the cent, which under the arithmetic-outranks-glyphs rule settles the readings. THE ONE GENUINELY DOUBTFUL GLYPH is the hundreds digit of the Summary Page's line 2 (5 vs 6, both columns): it was NOT resolved by re-rendering but by the document's own arithmetic — the 42 expenditure rows sum to 6,657.58 and the balance ladder closes only at 6,657.58, so that is the reading. Three tight crops were taken and are recorded in the frames as geometry proofs, including the deliberate split of a doubled band on p5.

3.measure_note: NOT the county underline form — the filer's own typed, fully BOXED spreadsheet, so a row lies BETWEEN its own two rules (not above one). rowbands.py returns a complete 50-rule ladder at pitch 1.83 with no gaps and four vertical rules giving the columns directly (date 4.88-15.59, donor 15.59-41.80, location 41.80-78.41, amount 78.41-89.97, the last split internally by a rule at 79.85 that separates the printed '$' from the figure — the stored band deliberately includes the '$'). The first gap [5.12,7.06] is the printed COLUMN HEADER row ('date | donor | location | amount'), so data row k = [rule k, rule k+1] for k=1..47 and the last gap [93.26,95.02] is the subtotal row. THREE-CROP PROOF at 1400 dpi --value: row 1 pct:79.0,7.06,12.0,1.79@p3 rendered '$ 5.00' (the recorded row-1 amount, and the §A1 first-entry control — the filer began on the first line under the header); row 47 pct:79.0,91.33,12.0,1.93@p3 rendered '$ 10.00' (the recorded last row); and the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:79.0,93.26,12.0,1.76@p3 rendered '$ 1,894.78' — the printed page subtotal, which equals the sum of the 47 rows above it (§H4), not a 48th entry.

4.measure_note: Second page of the same typed boxed ledger; 34 rules at pitch 1.83, no gaps. First gap [5.01,6.92] is the column header, data rows are gaps 1..30, and the last two gaps are the 'subtotal' row [61.99,63.75] and the 'Total Contributions Received' row [63.75,65.70]. THREE-CROP PROOF at 1400 dpi --value: row 1 pct:79.0,6.92,12.0,1.82@p4 rendered '$ 10.00'; row 30 pct:79.0,60.06,12.0,1.93@p4 rendered '$ 1,000.00' (the last transcribed row, the Ann Bryner in-kind videos); and the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:79.0,61.99,12.0,1.76@p4 rendered '$ 5,385.36' — the printed page subtotal, equal to the 30 rows above it, not a 31st entry.

5.measure_note: The expenditure ledger — same typed boxed form but only THREE columns (date 7.77-20.50, vendor 20.50-76.41, amount 76.41-89.26): there is NO address column and NO purpose column on it. ⚠ rowbands.py MISSED ONE RULE and returned a DOUBLE BAND: the detected list jumps 62.39 -> 66.03, a gap of 3.64 against a pitch of 1.83 (the §F6 hazard). The missing rule was interpolated at 64.21 and the band SPLIT, giving 44 rules = 1 header gap + 42 data rows. THE SPLIT WAS CROP-PROVED, and this is the case that shows why the check matters: BOTH halves render a figure — pct:78.0,62.39,12.0,1.82@p5 rendered '$ 105.42' and pct:78.0,64.21,12.0,1.82@p5 rendered '$ 105.42' — because the ledger really does carry two consecutive PG Printers charges of the same amount on 1-Sep-18 and 8-Sep-18. Taking the doubled band as one row would have dropped 105.42 and put the side 105.42 short of its printed total; splitting it closes the side exactly. FURTHER PROOF at 1400 dpi --value: row 1 pct:78.0,9.26,12.0,1.82@p5 rendered '$ 20.84'; row 42 pct:78.0,84.39,12.0,1.91@p5 rendered '$ 43.58'; and the §B5 one-past-the-end control pct:78.0,86.30,12.0,1.82@p5 rendered '$ 6,657.58' — the printed 'Total Expenditures', equal to the 42 rows above it, not a 43rd entry.

notes: PAGE-FACE candidate 'Teri McCabe' (handwritten), party 'United Utah' — a third-party candidate, the only one in this chunk — residence Provo; Office Seeking written 'Utah County Commissioner Seat A', which agrees with index.csv's channel label. index.csv names no candidate; the page face supplies it. Report type 'Seven days preceding the General Election'; amendment 'No'; signed and dated 27 Oct 2018; the clerk's received mark is a faint bleed-through stamp reading OCT 29 PM 12:57 and the 'For Office Use Only' box itself is empty. FORM STOCK: the cover is the common blank titled 'FINANCIAL CAMPAIGN REPORT FOR COUNTY & LOCAL SCHOOL BOARD CANDIDATES' (Code 2-5 & 17-16-6.5 & 20A-11-13) while the ONE county inner sheet — the Summary Page — is strap-lined '2016 County & Local School Board Candidates', i.e. LEFTOVER 2016 STOCK inside a genuinely 2018 filing (`utah-template-vintage-year`; the year is not reclassified and this is not a bound-in prior report). Its Page/of, Last Name and Date of Report boxes are all BLANK. DOCUMENT SHAPE: 5 pages = cover / Summary Page / the filer's own typed Schedule A ledger page 1/2 / page 2/2 / her own typed Schedule B ledger page 1/1, each of the three ledgers hand-headed in ink with its schedule name and its own 'page n/m'. The county's Schedule A and Schedule B FORMS are absent, but the entries are not, so both sides are `transcribed` and neither is `no-schedule-page` (§A2/§E5). Unusually for this chunk, the Summary Page IS present, so both sides gate on a genuine Column A as well as on the ledgers' own footers, and all four figures agree. ⚠ SCOPE: the ledgers open on 11-Nov-17 and run to 24-Oct-18, i.e. they restate the whole cycle rather than one reporting period, and Column B prints the same figure as Column A. Since Column A is what the filer certified and the ledgers close on it exactly, the side is `exact` — but a reader must not add this filing's totals to another McCabe report as if they were disjoint increments. THE IN-KIND FINDING IS THE HEADLINE: three gifts are entered TWICE, once as a contribution and once as an offsetting expenditure of identical date and amount, and both stated Column A figures include them — the same double-entry convention §G1 records for Voeks 2016, occurring here in 2018, while ANOTHER 2018 Commission filing in this very chunk (Ellingson) excludes its single in-kind row from Column A. Two filings, one cycle, one office, opposite conventions. DATE FORMAT — WORTH FLAGGING DOWNSTREAM: every date on all three ledgers is typed in the spreadsheet form `D-Mon-YY` ('11-Nov-17', '5-May-18'), which is NOT one of the separator forms the build's normalizer is documented to parse (M/D/YY(YY) with / - or .). The dates are complete and unambiguous and are recorded verbatim as the contract requires; if they normalize to blank downstream that is a parser gap, not a transcription gap. ROW-INDEX TRAPS SCREENED: on all three ledgers the first data row sits directly under the printed column header (crop-proved), there is no banner, voided or continuation line, the one-past-the-end control rendered a printed subtotal or total on every page and never a further entry, and the ONE doubled band — p5's merged 62.39-66.03 — was split and BOTH halves crop-proved to distinct real rows (§F6/§H3). FIELD-SHIFT SCREEN: the ledgers print their own column headers and every cell's content matches its header, with two benign exceptions recorded on the rows themselves (a location cell holding 'Paypal donation' instead of an address, and a location cell holding only a state name). PRIVACY: this filing is NOT redacted and prints full street lines for most donors; every one was reduced to city/state at READ TIME and no street line was carried into any field or note. The Schedule B ledger carries no address column at all, so no vendor location exists to reduce.
